chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Salih ibn al-Sindi, from one of his men, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

We were in his presence, and they mentioned the water on the road to Mecca and its heaviness. So he said: 'The water is not heavy unless the camel is unique with it, so there does not happen to be upon it except for the water.'

key_terms.يَنْفَرِدَ بِهِ: To be unique with it / sole cargo

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on water carried by camels in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the economic principle regarding the 'weight' of water carried by camels on the route to Mecca, likely in the context of trade or zakat calculations. He establishes that water is not considered a heavy burden (thiqal) affecting the camel's load value unless it constitutes the sole cargo, thereby distinguishing between incidental transport and dedicated water carriage. This ruling reflects the practical jurisprudence of the Abbasid era, where water scarcity and transport logistics significantly influenced commercial tax assessments.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Salih Bin Al Sandy, from one of his men, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘We were in his<sup>asws</sup> presence, and they (people) mentioned the water in the road of Makkah, and its heavy (flooding). So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The water is not heavy unless the camel is unique with it, so there does not happen to be upon it except for the water’.
en.sarwar: 8. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from Salih ibn al-Sindiy from certain individuals of his people who has said the following:

“We once were in the presence of abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, and people mentioned water on the way to Makkah and that it is heavy. He (the Imam) said, ‘Water is not heavy unless there is just the camel and there is nothing on it except water.’”
